newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Southern Glass lauds bond issue.
newsitem.headline: China Southern Glass lauds bond issue.

text.p: China Southern Glass Holdings Co Ltd has seen more than 60 percent of its US$45 million B share convertible bonds, issued in 1995, converted into B shares, a company spokesman said on Monday.
"Our bond issue is a success given the proportion of bonds converted into the firm's B shares in the past 20 months," he told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.
More than $28 million in bonds have so far been converted into about 65 million of the firm's B shares, the spokesman said.
Southern Glass issued $45 million worth of five-year B share convertible bonds to foreign investors in July 1995, according to the spokesman.
"We expect the rest of the bonds to be converted into our B shares by maturity," the official said.
Southern Glass has injected the $45 million raised from the bond issue into its 1.1-billion-yuan float glass plant, which began operation last December, he said.
The plant is expected to turn out 135,000 tonnes of glass products worth 500 million yuan per year once it begins full operations, according to the official.
Profits from the plant will be limited in 1997 as it will operate on a trial basis, but it is expected to become one of the company's main sources of profit over the next few years, he said.
Southern Glass posted net profits of 153.04 million yuan for 1996, compared with 127 million in 1995 based on international accounting standards.
The rise was a result of the company successfully limiting production costs, according to its 1996 annual report.
